issues.description: The problem statement requires a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String name (SealSaloon(String)) for identification, but the provided solution (and the template's commented usage) use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This mismatch between the specification and the implementation can confuse students about the required constructor signature and the presence of a saloon name field/getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent with the specification. Either update the implementation (and template usage) to provide public SealSaloon(String name), store the name in a private field, and add a getter for it, or modify the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor. Preferably implement SealSaloon(String) and ensure Main and tests use the same constructor form.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) requires a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but both the provided template usage and the solution implement and use a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon()). This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and where to put initialization logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor, or change the template and solution to implement SealSaloon(String name) (and update Main to call new SealSaloon("name")). Ensure the constructor signature and example usage match in problem_statement.md, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, and src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java.
